findings.reason: a worker bound to these paths must either synthesise a second claim writer outside the module that owns the record or report a scope blocker, and both outcomes are avoidable by granting `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py`.
findings.text: done-when case 3 requires `claim.json` to name the launching pid, host and step reached, but the only writer of that file is `_publish_launch_claim` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:856`, writing the two-field record at :912), and the release named in the deliverable is `_release_launch_claim` at :918 in the same module; `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` only re-exports both (lines 175, 3807-3815), so the section's write paths (`dispatch.py`, `queue_admission.py`, `dispatch_claims.py`-free) cannot produce the claim record its third case asserts

findings.reason: without a fence the release either produces a false refusal beside a live worker or refuses a run that then launches anyway, so the repair must add the check the holder reads at the pre-spawn boundary and case 1 must assert the held launch does not later spawn.
findings.text: the deliverable makes the admit service's pass release the claim and remove the run directory after the bound, but the holder is a live process blocked inside the span (the section's own Why: the follower "never ended", it blocked in a GPFS `git` read) and the launch path checks only a discard record before the spawn (`_refuse_a_discarded_launch`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:942`, called at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3503/3507/3561`), so a release it does not read leaves the holder free to wake, write the supervisor spec into the directory just removed, spawn the worker and re-publish the pointer via `_mutate_pointer`, which is the duplicate-launch hazard `_publish_launch_claim`'s own docstring exists to prevent

findings.reason: the case is the only evidence the refusal mechanism works, and it cannot distinguish a launch that was stopped from one that was merely refused on paper.
findings.text: case 1 asserts the released claim, the removed run directory and the recorded refusal, but nothing in it observes the holder, so a release racing a still-live launch passes the case while leaving the defect the deliverable claims to fix

findings.reason: the done-when already separates them into distinct cases with distinct negative controls, so the gate can fail one half on its own and splitting would add a node without changing what is built.
